parsed.explanation: Traveler-facing positives dominate the documented record: gender identity/expression are protected grounds nationally and provincially with a functioning complaints route, hate-motivation provisions are in the criminal code (2017), national documents offer an X marker, most provinces use self-declaration recognition, and no border-screening, facility-exclusion or universal-exposure practice is documented. Custody placement follows gender identity. Against that: hate crimes have risen six consecutive years, an organised anti-trans movement is documented, and two provinces enacted pronoun/healthcare rollbacks with override clauses — but those are school/resident-facing, not visitor exposures. The 39% survey figure is 2SLGBTQI+-wide and 90% verbal, so limited weight as trans-specific visitor prevalence. The anonymous jurisdiction's worst features are rising social hostility with legal protections that operate — tier 3 territory with recourse — not tier 1 state-imposed exposure.
